summary_zh: 用 must have／can't have／might have 推測視訊會議上「剛剛到底發生了什麼事」，並學會講斷線、靜音、延遲等狀況的說法。

vocab.definition: with your microphone switched off, so other people on the call cannot hear you
vocab.example: Sorry, I was on mute. Could you repeat the question?
vocab.example_zh: 抱歉，我剛剛是靜音。可以再問一次嗎？

vocab.definition: if someone's voice breaks up on a call, you only hear parts of what they say
vocab.example: You're breaking up a bit. Can you move closer to your router?
vocab.example_zh: 你的聲音有點斷斷續續的，可以靠近路由器一點嗎？

vocab.zh: 延遲；畫面或聲音跟不上
vocab.definition: a delay between when something happens and when you see or hear it
vocab.example: There's a two-second lag, so let's not interrupt each other.
vocab.example_zh: 有兩秒的延遲，所以我們不要互相打斷。

vocab.definition: to let other people on a video call see what is on your computer screen
vocab.example: Let me screen-share the dashboard so we're all looking at the same numbers.
vocab.example_zh: 我來分享螢幕給大家看儀表板，這樣大家看的是同一組數字。

vocab.definition: to leave a call and join it again, usually to fix a technical problem
vocab.example: My video froze, so I'm going to drop off and dial back in.
vocab.example_zh: 我的畫面卡住了，我先離開再重新加入。

vocab.definition: when two or more people speak at the same time and nobody can be heard clearly
vocab.example: We kept talking over each other, so Lena asked everyone to raise a hand first.
vocab.example_zh: 我們一直同時講話，所以 Lena 請大家先舉手再發言。

vocab.zh: 常出小毛病的；不穩定的
vocab.definition: often having small technical problems that stop something from working properly
vocab.example: The meeting app has been glitchy all week, so keep the dial-in number handy.
vocab.example_zh: 這個會議軟體整個禮拜都不太穩，所以撥入號碼要放在手邊。

vocab.definition: to find out why something is not working and try to fix it
vocab.example: IT spent an hour trying to troubleshoot my headset before they gave me a new one.
vocab.example_zh: IT 花了一個小時想找出我耳機的問題，最後直接給我一副新的。

reading.title: What Went Wrong on Monday's Client Call
paragraphs: Monday's call with the Osaka team was supposed to take thirty minutes. It took almost an hour, and we only got through half the agenda, so the last three items will carry over to Thursday. Here is what happened, and what we can do differently.

First, Ken's audio kept breaking up. At first we blamed the client's connection, but the people in Osaka could hear each other perfectly, so the problem must have been on our side. Ken later found out that his laptop had been downloading a huge update in the background. That also explains the lag: his video was about three seconds behind his voice.

Then Maya tried to screen-share the sales figures, but the client only saw a blank window. She might have shared the wrong screen, or the app might have blocked it. Either way, she ended up dialing back in to fix it, and we lost another five minutes. While we waited, two of us started talking over each other, which didn't help.

Finally, Sam was on mute for his entire update. He can't have noticed the red microphone icon, because he talked for two full minutes before anyone could tell him, even though the icon is easy to spot at a glance. To be fair, he was feeling run-down and had taken some over-the-counter cold medicine that morning.

None of this was anyone's fault. Video tools are simply glitchy sometimes. But a few habits would help: close large downloads before a call, do a quick screen-share test before the meeting starts, and if something goes wrong, don't troubleshoot for ten minutes in front of the client. Drop off, fix it, and come back.

questions.q: Why does the writer think the audio problem was on their own side?
options: Because Ken's headset was old
Because the people in Osaka could hear each other without any problem
Because the client complained about the sound
Because Maya's screen share had also failed
questions.explain_zh: 第二段：the people in Osaka could hear each other perfectly, so the problem must have been on our side。對方彼此聽得很清楚，所以推斷問題在自己這邊。

questions.q: What did the client see when Maya tried to share the sales figures?
options: The wrong spreadsheet
A frozen video of Maya
A blank window
Last month's figures
questions.explain_zh: 第三段：the client only saw a blank window。至於原因，作者只是推測（might have shared the wrong screen），並不確定。

questions.q: Why does the writer most likely mention Sam's cold medicine?
options: To explain why Sam missed the call completely
To suggest that Sam should see a doctor
To give a reason why Sam didn't notice he was on mute
To show that the meeting was too long
questions.explain_zh: 推論題。第四段先說 Sam 一直沒發現自己靜音，接著用 To be fair 帶出他身體不舒服、吃了感冒藥，意思是替他找個情有可原的理由。他並沒有錯過會議，所以 A 不對。

grammar.point: Modals of deduction: must have, can't have, might have
grammar.point_zh: 推測過去：must have／can't have／might have + 過去分詞

guide.key_zh: 看證據推測過去：確定有＝must have，確定沒有＝can't have，可能＝might have，接 p.p.。

uses.note_zh: 根據眼前的證據推出結論

uses.label_zh: 幾乎確定沒發生（不可能）
uses.signal: there's no way, impossible, he wasn't even…

uses.note_zh: may have／could have 意思相近

mistakes.wrong: He must have forgot to unmute.
mistakes.right: He must have forgotten to unmute.
mistakes.why_zh: have 後面要接過去分詞（forgotten），不是過去式（forgot）

mistakes.wrong: She might has left the call.
mistakes.right: She might have left the call.
mistakes.why_zh: 情態動詞後面一律接原形 have，不會變成 has

mistakes.wrong: He must have heard me — he wasn't even in the meeting.
mistakes.right: He can't have heard me — he wasn't even in the meeting.
mistakes.why_zh: 證據（他根本不在會議裡）表示「不可能」，要用 can't have + p.p.；must have 是「一定有」，意思正好相反

examples.en: Ken's icon suddenly went gray. He must have lost his connection.
examples.zh: Ken 的頭像突然變灰色，他一定是斷線了。

examples.en: Sam can't have heard the question. He was still on another call.
examples.zh: Sam 不可能聽到那個問題，他那時還在另一通電話上。

examples.en: I'm not sure why the slides didn't load. Maya might have shared the wrong window.
examples.zh: 我不確定投影片為什麼沒出來，Maya 可能分享錯視窗了。

exercises.q: The client's video froze and then disappeared from the screen. They ___ (I'm sure / lose) their connection.
exercises.explain_zh: 頭像變灰＋聲音斷掉是很明確的證據，「一定是」→ must have + p.p.。lose 的過去分詞是 lost。

exercises.q: Lena left the call before we discussed the budget, so she ___ (it's impossible / hear) the decision.
exercises.explain_zh: 她在討論預算前就離開了，所以「不可能聽到」→ can't have + p.p.：can't have heard。

exercises.q: I'm not sure why the client saw a blank window. Maya ___ (maybe / share) the wrong screen.
exercises.explain_zh: I'm not sure 表示不確定，只是「有可能」→ might have + p.p.：might have shared。

exercises.q: There was a loud echo during the whole call. Someone ___ (I'm sure / forget) to put on their headphones.
exercises.explain_zh: 整通電話都有回音，幾乎可以確定有人沒戴耳機 → must have + p.p.。forget 的過去分詞是 forgotten，不是 forgot。

exercises.q: Mark joined the call right on time, so he ___ the wrong link. The problem must be something else.
options: must have gotten
can't have gotten
might get
can't get
exercises.explain_zh: 他準時進了會議，所以「不可能拿到錯的連結」→ can't have + p.p.。must have gotten 意思相反；might get 和 can't get 講的是現在或未來，不是推測過去。

exercises.q: I don't know why Amy dropped off. Her laptop battery ___, or maybe her Wi-Fi went down.
options: must have died
can't have died
might have died
might died
exercises.explain_zh: 後面接 or maybe 列出另一個可能，表示說話者不確定 → might have + p.p.。must have 太肯定；might died 少了 have。

review.point: Gerund vs infinitive: stop doing / stop to do, remember, try
review.point_zh: 動名詞 vs 不定詞：stop／remember／try 後面接 V-ing 或 to V，意思不一樣

exercises.q: Please remember ___ (unmute) yourself before you start your update on Thursday.
exercises.explain_zh: Thursday 還沒到，是提醒「別忘了要去做」→ remember to V：to unmute。

exercises.q: My video kept freezing, so I tried ___ (turn) off my camera, and the audio got much better.
exercises.explain_zh: 關掉鏡頭是「試一個方法看看有沒有效」，後面 the audio got much better 就是結果 → try V-ing：turning。

exercises.q: Halfway through her presentation, Maya stopped ___ (answer) a question from the chat, and then she went back to her slides.
exercises.explain_zh: 她是在簡報中途「停下來，為了去回答」聊天室的問題，接著又回到投影片 → stop to V：to answer。stopped answering 是「不再回答」，和後面 went back to her slides 的語意不合。

guide.key_zh: stop／remember：V-ing＝在做或做過，to V＝接著要做。try：V-ing＝試方法，to V＝努力做到。

uses.label_zh: stop：停掉正在做的事 vs 停下來去做另一件事
uses.note_zh: stop to V 的 to＝為了去做

uses.label_zh: remember：記得做過 vs 記得要去做
uses.note_zh: V-ing＝過去的回憶；to V＝還沒做、別忘了

uses.label_zh: try：試試看某個方法 vs 努力想做到
uses.note_zh: try V-ing＝實驗看看有沒有效；try to V＝想辦法完成（不容易）

mistakes.wrong: Remember locking the door when you leave tonight.
mistakes.right: Remember to lock the door when you leave tonight.
mistakes.why_zh: tonight 還沒發生，是提醒要去做的事 → remember to V

mistakes.wrong: I stopped to check my phone during meetings because it was rude.
mistakes.right: I stopped checking my phone during meetings because it was rude.
mistakes.why_zh: 因為覺得沒禮貌，所以「戒掉、不再做」這個習慣 → stop V-ing；stop to check 是「停下來去看手機」，和 because it was rude 的邏輯不合

questions.explain_zh: Ken 說：The mic kept cutting out even after the update finished，換了插孔也沒改善，所以買新的。

To show Maya the price

questions.q: What does Maya tell Ken to do if the problem comes back on Thursday?

Switch to a different headset
Ask IT to troubleshoot during the call
Turn off his camera

prompts.question: Your coworker's video suddenly freezes and their voice stops. In one or two sentences, guess what happened, using "must have" or "might have".
prompts.question_zh: 同事的畫面突然卡住、聲音也沒了。用 must have 或 might have 說一兩句你的推測。用安靜模式打字也算。
prompts.sample: She must have lost her connection. Her Wi-Fi might have gone down.

prompts.question: You join a call and nobody seems to hear you. Ask politely in the chat if they can hear you, starting with "Could you tell me…" or "Do you know if…".
prompts.question_zh: 你加入會議，但好像沒人聽得到你。在聊天室用 Could you tell me… 或 Do you know if… 開頭，禮貌地問大家聽不聽得到。
prompts.sample: Could you tell me if you can hear me? I think I might be on mute.

writing.task: Yesterday's video call with a client went badly. Write a short message to your team in three short parts: (1) what went wrong, (2) what probably caused it (use "must have" or "might have"), and (3) what will happen next and one thing everyone should do before the next call. Don't join two complete sentences with only a comma.
writing.task_zh: 昨天和客戶的視訊會議很不順。寫一則短訊息給團隊，分三小段：(1) 出了什麼問題；(2) 推測原因（用 must have 或 might have）；(3) 接下來怎麼辦，以及下次開會前大家要做的一件事。不要只用逗號把兩個完整的句子接在一起。
writing.sample:
Hi team,

Yesterday's call with the client didn't go well. My audio kept cutting out, and the client couldn't see our slides for almost five minutes.

I checked my laptop afterward. A big update must have been running in the background. The slides problem is less clear. I might have shared the wrong window, or the app might have blocked it.

We didn't finish the agenda, so the last two items will carry over to Friday's call. Before Friday, please close any large downloads and test your screen share. If your connection drops, don't try to fix it during the call. Just leave and dial back in.

Thanks,
Ken
checklist_zh: 三小段都有寫到：問題、原因、下一步
must have／might have 後面接過去分詞（lost、shared、been），不是過去式
四個指定用語都有用上
沒有只用逗號把兩個完整句子接在一起

reading.title: The All-Hands That Wasn't
paragraphs: At 9:58 last Wednesday, roughly 1,200 people clicked the same link to hear the CEO announce the company's new strategy. By 10:03, about a third of them were staring at a spinning wheel. The video stuttered, the slides lagged a full sentence behind the speaker, and the chat filled up with the same question in a dozen forms: "Is it just me?" It wasn't.

The post-mortem published by IT on Friday is refreshingly candid. The platform itself held up fine, the team concluded; the bottleneck was closer to home. Because the event was scheduled for the start of the working day, it collided with hundreds of laptops still syncing backups that should have finished overnight, and the office's shared connection simply buckled under the load. Remote staff, who weren't competing for the same pipe, mostly had a smooth experience, which is what first tipped off the investigators.

What the report doesn't say outright, but strongly implies, is that the warning signs had been there for months. Smaller meetings had been glitchy at that hour for a while, and people had quietly adapted, switching off their cameras or dialing in by phone rather than raising a ticket. Each workaround made sense on its own; together, they hid a problem that was only ever going to surface when everyone showed up at once.

The fixes are mostly unglamorous: backups will now run at 3 a.m., large events will be streamed rather than hosted as interactive calls, and anyone who works around a recurring tech problem is being asked to report it anyway. The CEO, for her part, has agreed to re-record the announcement. As one engineer put it, "If we'd caught this in June, nobody would have had to sit through a strategy talk twice."

questions.q: How did IT first realize the problem wasn't the video platform itself?
options: The platform company told them it was working normally
Remote employees had few problems, while people in the office had many
The CEO's slides loaded correctly on her own laptop
The chat function kept working during the outage
questions.explain_zh: 第二段：Remote staff… mostly had a smooth experience, which is what first tipped off the investigators。在家的人都很順，在辦公室的人才卡，所以調查人員發現問題出在公司網路。

questions.q: What does the writer suggest about the employees' workarounds before the event?
options: They caused the backups to run during the day
They were against company rules
They kept a long-standing problem hidden from IT
They solved the problem for most meetings
questions.explain_zh: 推論題。第三段：大家自己關鏡頭、改用電話撥入而不報修，together, they hid a problem…，也就是這些權宜之計讓 IT 一直沒發現問題。

questions.q: What does the engineer's comment at the end imply?
options: The CEO's talk was too long
The problem could have been found and fixed months earlier
The engineers had warned management in June
Employees enjoyed hearing the strategy twice
questions.explain_zh: 推論題。If we'd caught this in June 是「如果六月就發現的話」，暗示問題早就存在、本來可以更早修好。文中沒說工程師六月就警告過（C）。

listening.title: Talking through the post-mortem

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Okay, so, before we start, did everyone read the post-mortem? Or at least skim it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Tom
lines.text: I skimmed it. Honestly, I'm a bit surprised it was the backups. I'd have bet money on the platform.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Same. But it can't have been the platform. The remote folks were totally fine.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Tom
lines.text: Right, right. Although, hang on, some of the remote people complained too, didn't they?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: A handful, yeah. But they might have just had bad Wi-Fi at home. It wasn't a pattern.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Tom
lines.text: Fair enough. What gets me is the part about people turning their cameras off for months.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: I know. I'm guilty of that myself, to be honest. I just assumed it was my laptop.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Tom
lines.text: We all did. Which is kind of the point, isn't it? Nobody flagged it, so nobody fixed it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Exactly. So, going forward, if something keeps happening, even if you've found a way around it, log it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Tom
lines.text: Even the tiny stuff? Like, the echo in Room 4?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Especially the tiny stuff. That echo has been there since I joined.

questions.q: What is the main lesson Priya wants the team to take away?
options: Always keep your camera on in meetings
Report recurring problems even if you have a workaround

glossary.definition: a meeting or report that looks at why something went wrong after it has happened
honest and direct, even about things that are uncomfortable
to stop working properly because of too much pressure or weight

glossary.zh: 讓某人察覺；給某人線索
glossary.definition: to give someone a clue or warning that helps them notice something
not exciting or impressive, but often useful

replies.zh: 今天翻譯第 3 題放了一組對照：has been testing（整個早上一直在做、還在進行）vs has already tested three（已經完成、有數量的結果），練習自己寫出兩種形式。
